items.name: block-typography
items.title: Slide typography
items.description: Two primitives every other block builds on. Eyebrow is an uppercase accent label at --slide-label-size with --slide-label-tracking letter spacing, in --primary. SlideHeading is an h1 at --slide-heading-size capped at 1500 canvas pixels, with an optional lead paragraph at --slide-lead-size in --muted-foreground capped at 1100. Both read the theme's size tokens rather than Tailwind text sizes, so they resize when you retune the type scale, and both name their parts: data-slide-eyebrow, data-slide-title, and data-slide-lead. Reach for them when you are writing your own slide layout and want the deck's heading rhythm without copying class strings. Every other Deckard block depends on this item.

items.name: block-slide-layouts
items.title: Slide layouts
items.description: The whole-slide frames a deck reaches for most, all left aligned and filling the padded frame except the two that centre. HeroSlide runs the height of the frame with the eyebrow on the top edge and the title block on the bottom one at --slide-title-size, takes an optional meta array for a credit row, and puts the free height above the title. HeroSplitSlide is the same opener with the credit line stood up as a definition list in a fixed --slide-rail-size column, for a title that runs three lines. HeroCenteredSlide is the centered opener, with an optional pill badge above the title. BreakerSlide is a section divider with an optional index string themes set oversized; MinimalBreakerSlide is the centered one, a short accent rule and a title. StatementSlide is one sentence at --slide-title-size over a rule with a mono attribution under it, marked up as a paragraph rather than an h1, so a theme that sets headings in capitals leaves it alone; pair it with background: "accent". CodeSplitSlide puts a block on the left and a numbered rail of notes on the right, taking the block as children, so it imports no CodeBlock of its own and you pass one in. ContentSlideCard puts an eyebrow, heading, and lead above a bordered --slide-surface panel, for body content with no surface of its own; OpenContentSlide is the same intro with no panel, for content that brings its own frame; FocusSlide hands one block the whole frame at the normal type scale, with an optional kicker under it. Every frame with a title pulls it from useSlideTitle() when you do not pass one. They respect --slide-content-gap, --slide-item-gap, --slide-rail-size, --slide-radius, --slide-radius-lg, --slide-surface, --slide-surface-border, and --slide-surface-shadow, and they name their parts with data-slide-hero, data-slide-hero-meta, data-slide-badge, data-slide-rail, data-slide-rail-term, data-slide-rail-detail, data-slide-breaker, data-slide-breaker-index, data-slide-accent-rule, data-slide-statement, data-slide-statement-text, data-slide-statement-source, data-slide-split, data-slide-split-main, data-slide-split-aside, data-slide-note, data-slide-note-index, data-slide-note-text, data-slide-intro, data-slide-panel, and data-slide-kicker, which is how a theme swap restyles them with no edits.

items.name: block-collections
items.title: Slide collections
items.description: Collections for lists, reveals, contents, columns, and cards. RevealList wraps each item in SlideStep and owns its token-aware treatment, so the deck definition contains content rather than styling classes. BulletList numbers and rules each row. ContentsList pairs section names with authored numerals and folios. ColumnGrid lays parallel points out as ruled columns. FeatureGrid makes one row of cards, while CardGrid wraps cards across two or three columns and can mark one recommendation. These blocks name their parts with data-slide-* attributes and carry data-slide-surface, so compose them through OpenContentSlide or FocusSlide. They take plain arrays that a Server Component can load and pass straight in. None scrolls, so trim the copy when deckard check-overflow reports that a slide clips.

items.name: block-media
items.title: Slide media
items.description: Photo and video slides sized for the 1920x1080 canvas. FullscreenMediaSlide bleeds an image or a video to every edge and lays optional copy over the bottom on one of three scrims, from --slide-media-overlay-subtle to -strong; the framed variant insets it in a bordered surface instead. ImageShowcaseSlide is the split: copy left, media right on a 1fr to 1.05fr grid, caption under the media, centered inside the ordinary frame padding. Give it the normal layout, not fullscreen, which strips the gutters and leaves the image flush to the canvas edge. Its copy column carries no panel, so the media frame is the slide's one surface. MediaPair puts two captioned frames side by side and takes a tuple rather than an array, so a third frame is a compile error; reach for MediaGallery instead, which puts captioned frames on two or three columns and as many rows as the items need. All of them take next/image sources, forward blurDataURL from a static import when the source carries one, take unoptimized so an SVG served from public/ skips the image optimizer instead of needing dangerouslyAllowSVG, and use SlideMediaVideo from @thebuilder/deckard-core so video pauses on slides the audience is not looking at. The full bleed and grid layouts pad against --slide-chrome-top and --slide-chrome-bottom, so the deck header and slide counter never sit on top of a caption. They name their parts: data-slide-media, data-slide-media-item, data-slide-media-frame, data-slide-media-overlay, data-slide-media-caption, and data-slide-media-credit. Use these instead of dropping an img on a slide, which will not fit the canvas and will not respect the chrome.

items.name: block-metrics
items.title: Slide metrics
items.description: One export, StatGrid, for the figures slide every deck reaches for once. It takes two, three, or four stats, typed as a union of tuples, so a fifth is a compile error and a lone figure is too, and marks them up as a description list that splits into as many equal columns as it was given. At five figures, reach for DataTable in block-tables. Each column is a figure at --slide-figure-size in --slide-font-heading, an optional unit suffix at --slide-figure-unit-size, an optional meter bar at --slide-meter-size showing a proportion between 0 and 1, a caption at --slide-support-size capped to 26 characters a line, and a 2px rule across the top in --slide-surface-border. It sets no color of its own, so the rule picks up the theme border weight, and it carries data-slide-surface, so a panel around it warns in development. In a FocusSlide, three numbers fill the canvas. Every part of a column is named for themes to reach: data-stat-grid, data-stat-item, data-stat-value, data-stat-unit, data-stat-meter, and data-stat-caption. Write a caption that gives the figure something to be measured against; the 26ch measure is sized for "up from 2.6k", not for a sentence. Leave the meter out unless you can say what it is a proportion of.

items.name: block-prose
items.title: Slide prose
items.description: The two layouts where running copy is the slide. QuoteSlide sets a pull quote at --slide-heading-size with the attribution on a 2px rule under it, and takes an optional portrait that stays at --slide-radius, so ledger keeps it square and meridian rounds it to a circle from its own stylesheet. It writes no quotation marks. A theme that wants them hangs them off data-slide-quote-text, the way phosphor hangs a [x] off a list marker. ProseSlide is the label rail layout: a fixed --slide-rail-size column on the left carrying a label and any support lines, and a title plus paragraphs on the right. It is the one place in the catalogue a measure is capped, at 1100 canvas pixels, because a paragraph running the full 1920 is unreadable. Both are whole-slide frames, so they go straight in a slide's body rather than inside OpenContentSlide, and neither carries data-slide-surface. They name data-slide-quote, -text, -attribution, -portrait, -name, -source, and data-slide-prose, -body, -paragraph, plus data-slide-rail, -term, and -detail, which they share with HeroSplitSlide, so one theme rule styles both rails. Reach for QuoteSlide when someone else's sentence is the argument and StatementSlide when it is yours.

items.name: block-tables
items.title: Slide tables
items.description: Three blocks for rows of records: a slide of numbers, a plan, and a log. DataTable takes columns and rows as plain arrays and marks a column numeric to set it right aligned, mono, and tabular in one flag; a row marked highlight takes --slide-accent-soft, for the total or the recommendation. Nothing caps the row count. How many fit depends on the theme's type scale, so run deck:check-overflow; four or five rows is what the source templates show. Timeline lays milestones out as columns on one rule, each with a date, a short label, and a line of detail, and marks a milestone that landed with data-slide-timeline-done rather than a colour of its own, so meridian fills the pill and ledger thickens the rule from their own stylesheets. LogList is timestamped rows with a status on the right, at three tones, for a build log or a rollout read back in order; phosphor brackets the status, and the words stay in the deck, because a theme styles parts and never adds content. All three carry data-slide-surface, so compose them through OpenContentSlide or FocusSlide rather than a ContentSlideCard, and all three take plain arrays a server component can await. They name data-slide-table, -head, -heading, -row, -highlight, -cell; data-slide-timeline, -item, -marker, -done, -date, -label, -detail; and data-slide-log, -row, -tone, -time, -message, -status. Reach for StatGrid instead when there are four figures and no rows to speak of.

items.name: preset-blocks
items.title: Deckard blocks
items.description: Every slide block in one add, plus the one stylesheet line a consumer cannot guess: the @import of @thebuilder/deckard-core/styles.css, which carries the slide token contract and registers the package's own Tailwind source so the runtime classes survive tree shaking. Use this once, right after installing @thebuilder/deckard-core, then write slides. The theme is not in here and does not need to be: the Deckard themes are named exports of @thebuilder/deckard-themes, so a deck picks one with an import rather than an install.
items.docs: The blocks land in app/slides/blocks/, and the stylesheet import above is the whole build wiring. @thebuilder/deckard-core ships compiled and its stylesheet registers its own Tailwind source, so there is no transpilePackages entry and no @source line for you to add. What is left is deck code: create deck/deck.ts, import a theme from @thebuilder/deckard-themes, pass it to defineDeck, then render the deck from app/slides/[id]/page.tsx with createSlideRoute from @thebuilder/deckard-core/next. Run deckard eject theme when you want that theme as three files in deck/theme/ you can edit.
